basis: Defining limb and skeletal malformations, nail dystrophy, and dental/oral abnormalities; cardiac abnormalities are specifically absent.
Cystic kidneys, CNS malformations and polydactyly define Meckel syndrome; hepatobiliary ductal malformation in 6/7. Cleft palate in 4/8 omitted by cap.
Defined by cone-rod retinal dystrophy and amelogenesis imperfecta affecting dental enamel.
Choriocarcinoma arising within the central nervous system.
Cervicofacial fibrocartilaginous lesion supports a musculoskeletal assignment; definition is absent and precise tissue compartment is uncertain.
Usually viral infection causing inflammation and obstruction of the larynx and adjacent conducting airways.
Mitochondrial myopathy, lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anemia define disease; intellectual disability in 1/2. Retinopathy in 1/2 omitted by cap; samples small.
Mitochondrial disorder defined here as IOSCA; optic atrophy and hearing impairment each 80-99%. Elevated liver enzymes alone do not establish hepatic damage.
Defining combination of femoral-head epiphyseal dysplasia, high myopia and hearing impairment.
Pituitary adenoma composed of growth-hormone-producing and prolactin-producing cells.
Bowel motility dysfunction producing diarrheal disease; no other organ damage is intrinsic to this concept.
Bladder and intestinal dysfunction define disease; pulmonary hypoplasia/bronchomalacia and aortic aneurysm/PDA each reported in 1/1. Hearing loss 1/1 omitted by cap; samples small.
Mitochondrial myopathy directly affecting extraocular and eyelid muscles, with progressive ocular immobility; broader complications vary across subtypes.
Fungal infection of the external ear canal.
Malignant neoplasm involving an upper-limb long bone.
Neurodevelopmental disease and anemia define syndrome; cataracts 4/5, retinal dystrophy 3/5 and hearing loss 2/5. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage.
Teratoma originating in ovary or testis; reproductive location without an intrinsic endocrine disorder.
Umbrella for neurological disorders of voluntary or involuntary movement; skeletal muscle damage is not intrinsic across the group.
Melanocytic neoplasm arising in the meninges; its site of origin is within the central nervous system.
Inherited isolated platelet disorder with thrombocytopenia and enlarged platelets.
Mesenchymal neoplasm arising in the small intestine.
Congenital middle-ear ossicular malformations causing conductive hearing impairment.
Mitochondrial myopathy with progressive extraocular muscle paralysis. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness without demonstrated direct pulmonary damage.
Congenital minicore myopathy with arthrogryposis and skeletal deformities; respiratory restriction reflects muscle/thoracic dysfunction without demonstrated lung damage.
Pilocytic astrocytoma arising in the cerebellum.
